plainLanguage: Celina moved to the 2024 International Residential Code in early 2026 (Ordinance 2026-003), with North Texas regional amendments; electrical work follows the 2023 NEC. Almost every new home is in a planned development (PD), which sets its own setbacks, garage and material rules, so give us your subdivision's PD number. A typical example PD uses 20 ft front, 5 ft side and 20 ft rear setbacks on 5,750-6,900 sq ft lots; we use those only until your PD is confirmed. Impact fees are large here: about $15,000-20,000 per home for water, wastewater and roads. Many Celina subdivisions are also in MUDs or PIDs, which add yearly assessments. Plan on an engineer-designed foundation because of expansive clay. Texas law stops the city from requiring a brick percentage, but your HOA likely still will.
